research.title: A Neural Algorithm of Artistic Style
research.authors: Leon A. Gatys, Alexander S. Ecker, Matthias Bethge
research.abstract: Shows how convolutional neural network feature representations can separate and recombine image content and artistic style. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.06576

research.title: A Survey of Large Language Models
research.authors: Wayne Xin Zhao et al.
research.abstract: Surveys large language model development, adaptation, evaluation, applications, and open research challenges. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.18223

research.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
research.authors: Diederik P. Kingma, Jimmy Ba
research.abstract: Introduces an adaptive first-order optimization method combining estimates of gradient moments for stochastic objective functions. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6980

research.title: Attention Is All You Need
research.authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Lukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
research.abstract: Introduces the Transformer architecture, which uses attention mechanisms instead of recurrent or convolutional sequence processing. The paper evaluates it on machine translation and parsing. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

research.title: Attention is Not All You Need: Pure Attention Loses Rank Doubly Exponentially with Depth
research.authors: Yihe Dong, Jean-Baptiste Cordonnier, Andreas Loukas
research.abstract: Analyzes rank behavior in pure self-attention networks and studies how skip connections and feed-forward layers affect representation collapse. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03404

research.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
research.authors: Diederik P. Kingma, Max Welling
research.abstract: Develops a variational inference approach that enables scalable learning in directed probabilistic models with continuous latent variables. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114

research.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
research.authors: Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova
research.abstract: Presents BERT, a language representation model pretrained with bidirectional context and adaptable to multiple language understanding tasks. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805

research.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
research.authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
research.abstract: Introduces residual connections that make very deep neural networks easier to optimize, with image recognition experiments on ImageNet and CIFAR. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03385

research.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
research.authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel
research.abstract: Formulates a generative modeling method that learns to reverse a gradual noising process and evaluates generated image quality. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239

research.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
research.authors: Tomas Mikolov, Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, Jeffrey Dean
research.abstract: Describes efficient architectures for learning distributed word representations from large text corpora. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.3781

research.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
research.authors: Ian J. Goodfellow et al.
research.abstract: Introduces an adversarial framework in which generative and discriminative models are trained together to learn a data distribution. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2661

research.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
research.authors: Jeffrey Pennington, Richard Socher, Christopher D. Manning
research.abstract: Introduces a word vector model that combines global corpus statistics with local context windows. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3092

research.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
research.authors: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Geoffrey E. Hinton
research.abstract: Reports a deep convolutional model for large-scale image classification and discusses design choices that improved benchmark performance. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0580

research.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
research.authors: Tom B. Brown et al.
research.abstract: Evaluates how scaling autoregressive language models affects zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot performance across language tasks. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165

research.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
research.authors: Edward J. Hu et al.
research.abstract: Proposes low-rank trainable updates for adapting large pretrained language models while keeping their original weights frozen. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685

research.title: Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning
research.authors: Barret Zoph, Quoc V. Le
research.abstract: Uses a recurrent controller trained with reinforcement learning to propose neural network architectures for a target task. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.01578

research.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
research.authors: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio
research.abstract: Introduces an attention-based translation model that learns to align source words with target words during translation. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0473

research.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
research.authors: Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, Kilian Q. Weinberger
research.abstract: Studies confidence calibration in modern neural networks and evaluates techniques for improving the match between confidence and accuracy. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599

research.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
research.authors: Volodymyr Mnih et al.
research.abstract: Explores deep neural networks that learn control policies from high-dimensional visual input using reinforcement learning. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.5602

research.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
research.authors: John Schulman, Filip Wolski, Prafulla Dhariwal, Alec Radford, Oleg Klimov
research.abstract: Introduces policy optimization methods that constrain updates to improve the stability and simplicity of reinforcement learning. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347

research.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
research.authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Kuttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktaschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela
research.abstract: Studies language generation that combines pretrained models with retrieved passages, evaluating the approach on knowledge intensive NLP tasks. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401

research.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
research.authors: Ilya Sutskever, Oriol Vinyals, Quoc V. Le
research.abstract: Presents an encoder-decoder neural network approach for mapping input sequences to output sequences, demonstrated on machine translation. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3215

research.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
research.authors: Jonathan Frankle, Michael Carbin
research.abstract: Investigates whether dense neural networks contain sparse subnetworks that can train effectively from their original initialization. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03635

research.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
research.authors: Olaf Ronneberger, Philipp Fischer, Thomas Brox
research.abstract: Presents a U-shaped convolutional network for biomedical image segmentation, designed to learn from relatively small annotated datasets. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04597

research.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
research.authors: Joseph Redmon, Santosh Divvala, Ross Girshick, Ali Farhadi
research.abstract: Frames object detection as a single regression problem and describes a unified model designed for real-time image processing. Open-access source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02640
